title: Copper physics
description: What copper is, as the engine works out a pcb's copper as an electrical network: its resistivity and how it changes with temperature, the temperature a pcb stands in, IPC-2221's current-carrying constants, and how finely the network is solved. Data, beside this class (#SECTION); the copper's thickness is the pcb's way of making, not this.

$schema.description: the schema this file is written to

source.description: where each value comes from: the standards and books it is read from

ambient.description: °C the pcb stands in: a resistance is given at it

capacity.description: IPC-2221's I = k·ΔT^riseExponent·A^areaExponent, A in square mils.

riseExponent.description: the power the temperature rise is raised to

areaExponent.description: the power the cross-section is raised to

squareMilsPerSquareMillimetre.description: square mils in a square millimetre: the formula's unit of area

carrying.description: the share of the current below which a piece is taken as carrying none of it

edgeHalvings.description: how many halvings find where a piece crosses an area's edge

solver.description: How the nodal equations are solved: conjugate gradients until the residual is this small, at most this many iterations for each node and these more.

tolerance.description: the residual the conjugate gradients stop at

iterationsPerNode.description: iterations allowed for each node of the network
